source.title: Anticorrelated Noise Injection for Improved Generalization
source.authors: Antonio Orvieto; Hans Kersting; F. Proske; F. Bach; Aurélien Lucchi

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; some figures are flattened into the text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether anticorrelated noise changes test error and measured Hessian trace relative to GD, SGD, and uncorrelated PGD, using a new optimization intervention and several model settings.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own comparisons of test error or accuracy and training Hessian trace. Cited prior work is not recorded as results. Figure curves without readable point values are described qualitatively, with numeric fields marked figure only.
record.test_reason: The CIFAR-10 experiments compare large-batch GD with batch-128 SGD over common epoch horizons and test whether anticorrelated noise recovers large-batch test accuracy. These results bear on V5, although batch size is not the paper's main question. Unscaled Hessian trace does not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report improved generalization with anticorrelated noise, theoretically connect Anti-PGD to Hessian-trace regularization, and prove a flatness preference in the widening-valley model. Their results do not establish a universal causal relationship between flatness and generalization.
record.recipe_differences: Adds anticorrelated artificial parameter noise between consecutive gradient steps; comparisons include uncorrelated PGD, GD, and SGD. The study does not reproduce the listed original-source interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on noise-injection level and learning rate in the plotted sweeps; on CIFAR 10, accuracy and Hessian trace are evaluated after stopping noise injection for convergence. The study reports recovery behavior when noise injection begins after epoch 75.

fits_no_version.finding: Anti-PGD lowers synthetic-problem test error and unscaled training Hessian trace; the CIFAR-10 experiments also associate lower trace with better test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Anticorrelated parameter noise can improve test performance and reduce unscaled Hessian trace in the tested models.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 162, 2022
record.problems: Real-data results are reported for a ResNet18-like CIFAR 10 model; multiple synthetic settings are also used. Most results are presented as plots without readable exact values in the supplied text. The CIFAR 10 setup uses very large batches for GD/PGD/Anti-PGD and stops noise injection to evaluate convergence; results therefore do not establish the catalog's random-label or width-sweep claims.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported numeric values can be reliably recovered from the flattened figure plots; qualitative outcomes are captured in the relevant rows.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizers and their tuning.
Language models, the workload-dependent batch threshold, longer-training remedies, learning-rate scaling with warmup, and normalization or conventional regularization changes.
Dropout and weight-decay removal or addition.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, its ranking of generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: The CIFAR-10 Anti-SGD comparison at batch sizes 128 and 1024: the authors state that injected anticorrelated noise works best at moderate batch sizes. Record this batch-dependent benefit separately; the supplied flattened curves do not establish exact accuracy differences.

record.verdict_notes: States of cannot_determine for rows linked to none concern the listed versions, not whether the paper reports an Anti-PGD advantage. CIFAR-10 provides a limited batch comparison rather than a systematic batch-size sweep; exact curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization versus natural-label generalization and chance-level test performance.
Width sweep past interpolation and test error as a function of width.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness perturbations and comparison to norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

relationships.condition: ResNet18-like CIFAR-10 classifier, ordinary large-batch GD versus batch-128 SGD at learning rate 0.05 with momentum 0.9 over common epoch horizons.
relationships.reason: R3 and R4 show poorer held-out accuracy for the large-batch GD solution than for small-batch SGD; R4 explicitly describes recovery from that poorer solution.
relationships.display_finding: Held-out accuracy was poorer for large-batch gradient descent than small-batch SGD, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: Large-batch CIFAR-10 training adapted with anticorrelated parameter noise.
relationships.reason: R3 reports eventual accuracy above SGD after stopping noise at epoch 250; R4 reports recovery close to SGD with noise started at epoch 75, supporting V5's recipe-dependent qualification.
relationships.display_finding: Adapting the timing of noise substantially or completely restored performance, but these comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
